PASSO 1: wann só pergunta (direta ou ind: STEP 1: English "when" has three German versions: «wann» only asks a question (direct or indirect); «wenn» is the "when" of something that repeats or hasn't happened yet — and it's also "if"; «als» is the "when" of a single event in the past. STEP 2: English "if" has two: «wenn» for a condition ("if it rains") and «ob» for "whether" ("I don't know if/whether he's coming"). STEP 3: tip: if you can replace "if" with "whether", it's «ob».

Weil: o verbo vai para o fim, passo a pa: Weil: the verb goes to the end, step by step
PASSO 1: «weil» (porque) abre uma frase: STEP 1: «weil» (because) opens a SUBORDINATE clause: one that depends on another. STEP 2: MAIN RULE: in a subordinate clause, the CONJUGATED verb goes to the END: «Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich krank bin» — literally "…because I sick am". STEP 3: the COMMA before «weil» is required. STEP 4: with a separable verb, the prefix rejoins the verb at the end: «weil ich früh aufstehe». With the Perfekt, the auxiliary comes last: «weil ich Fieber gehabt habe». With a modal: «weil ich arbeiten muss». STEP 5: if the subordinate clause COMES FIRST, the main clause starts with the VERB (the whole subordinate clause counts as position one): «Weil ich krank bin, bleibe ich zu Hause.» STEP 6: the difference from «denn»: «denn» (because, for) is a normal conjunction and doesn't change the word order: «Ich bleibe zu Hause, denn ich bin krank.»
em português a ordem das palavras não mu: English keeps the same word order after "because" ("because I am sick"). German sends the conjugated verb to the END after «weil»: «weil ich krank bin». If you want English-style order, use «denn» instead.
Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich bin krank.
Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich krank bin.
Depois de «weil», o verbo conjugado vai: After «weil», the conjugated verb goes to the end.
Weil ich bin krank, bleibe ich zu Hause.
Weil ich krank bin, bleibe ich zu Hause.
Verbo no fim da subordinada e, depois, a: Verb at the end of the subordinate clause, then the main clause starts with the verb.
Ich bin müde, weil ich stehe früh auf.
Ich bin müde, weil ich früh aufstehe.
O prefixo separável se junta ao verbo no: The separable prefix rejoins the verb at the end.

Dass: o «que» da frase subordinada, pass: Dass: the "that" of the subordinate clause, step by step
PASSO 1: «dass» (que) liga verbos de pen: STEP 1: «dass» (that) links verbs of thinking, saying, knowing and hoping to a subordinate clause: «Ich glaube, dass er kommt» (I think that he's coming). STEP 2: the RULE is the same as with «weil»: conjugated verb at the END, comma before. STEP 3: verbs that often come before «dass»: sagen, glauben, denken, meinen, wissen, hoffen. STEP 4: «wissen» is irregular: ich weiß, du weißt, er weiß, wir wissen. STEP 5: after adjectives and expressions: «Es ist schade, dass …» (it's a pity that…), «Ich bin sicher, dass …» (I'm sure that…). STEP 6: English often drops "that" ("I think he's coming"); German can drop «dass» too, but then the clause keeps normal order: «Ich glaube, er kommt.» With «dass», the verb goes to the end. STEP 7: SPELLING: «dass» (conjunction, with «ss») is not «das» (article or pronoun): «Ich glaube, dass er kommt» × «Das Buch ist gut».
Ich glaube, dass er kommt nicht.
Ich glaube, dass er nicht kommt.
O verbo conjugado fica no fim, depois de: The conjugated verb goes at the end, after «nicht».
«dass» (conjunção) leva «ss»; «das» é ar: «dass» (conjunction) has «ss»; «das» is an article or pronoun.
Er sagt, dass hat er keine Zeit.
Er sagt, dass er keine Zeit hat.

PASSO 1: as duas conjunções seguem a mes: STEP 1: both conjunctions follow the same order: subject, other elements and, at the END, the conjugated verb. STEP 2: with more than one verb, the conjugated one comes last: «weil ich nicht kommen kann» (modal last), «dass ich ihn gesehen habe» (auxiliary last). STEP 3: «Warum …?» (why) questions take an answer with «weil»: «Warum kommst du nicht? — Weil ich arbeiten muss.» STEP 4: the short answer «Weil …» can stand without the main clause, just like English "Because I have to work."

Glauben apresenta aqui o conteúdo de uma: «Glauben» introduces the content of a belief here: Ich glaube, dass er krank ist. The «dass» clause doesn't turn the belief into a proven fact.

Als introduz aqui um período passado úni: «Als» introduces a single past period here, the narrator's childhood. «Wenn» can express a condition or repetition, but it isn't the choice for a past period seen as one whole.
